_about: Hand-written text for make_electronics_bom.py: group titles, plain-language roles, part descriptions and notes. Prices, quantities, part numbers, stock and links come from the CSV files at run time, never from here (except the lines in not_in_component_total, which have no CSV row). 'lines' is keyed by the exact 'Ref' string of Rev3.0_BOM_Ozdisan_100pcs.csv; 'not_sourced' holds the schematic references that have no row there. 'substitute': true marks a line whose bought part differs from Rev3.0_BOM.csv; the script cross-checks this against the CSVs and warns on disagreement.

groups.title: Mains input, fuses and noise filter
groups.what_it_does: The 230 V mains enters the board here. Fuses and a surge absorber protect the oven, and a filter stops electrical noise from the heater switching from travelling back into the wall socket.

groups.title: Low-voltage power supply
groups.what_it_does: A sealed mains-to-5 V module powers the whole board. Two small converters then turn the 5 V into 3.3 V for the chips and 1.2 V for the core of the display controller.

groups.title: Heater switching and mains timing
groups.what_it_does: The processor turns the 1 kW heater on and off through an electronic power switch (a triac). Optical couplers keep the mains side electrically separated from the low-voltage side, and a detector tells the processor when the mains voltage crosses zero, so the heater is switched at the gentlest moment.

groups.title: Fan switching
groups.what_it_does: A small relay switches the oven's mains-powered fan. The processor drives the relay through a transistor.

groups.title: Processor and programming port
groups.what_it_does: The ESP32 module is the brain of the controller: it runs the temperature control, the touch screen and Wi-Fi. A 6-pin header lets a USB adapter load new software.

groups.title: Display controller
groups.what_it_does: The processor cannot drive a 7-inch screen on its own. A dedicated display chip keeps the whole picture in its own memory and sends it to the screen about 60 times a second; small resistors on the fast data lines keep the signals clean and reduce radio interference.

groups.title: Screen connection, backlight and touch
groups.what_it_does: Two flat-cable connectors link the board to the screen and to its touch layer. A small boost converter makes the roughly 9.6 V that lights the screen's LED backlight, with the brightness set by the display chip, and tiny protection diodes guard the touch lines (and the probe input) against static electricity.

groups.title: Temperature measurement
groups.what_it_does: A thermocouple probe in the oven produces a tiny voltage that grows with temperature. A precise 16-bit converter chip measures it, a small thermistor measures the terminal's own temperature to correct the reading, and filters remove noise picked up along the probe cable.

groups.title: Cooling and mechanical parts
groups.what_it_does: Metal hardware without electronics: the tall heatsink that carries the heat away from the heater switch, and the clips that hold the two replaceable glass fuses.

groups.title: Probe, heater and wire connections
groups.what_it_does: Items that are not soldered parts of the board: the temperature probe that goes into the oven, the heater element itself, and the bare pads where the mains and fan cables are soldered on.

F3.role: Main fuse: cuts the mains if the oven draws too much current

L40.part: 100 µH 5 A power choke (filter coil), radial
L40.role: Main noise-filter coil; carries the full heater current

C40.part: 1 µF 275 VAC X2 safety film capacitor
C40.role: Works with the filter coil to soak up mains noise

C1.part: 100 nF 275 VAC X2 safety film capacitor
C1.role: Soaks up higher-frequency noise between the two mains wires

RV1.part: Varistor (surge absorber), 275 VAC class, 14 mm disc
RV1.role: Clamps voltage spikes from the mains, such as lightning surges

F1.role: Protects the branch that feeds the 5 V power module
F1.note: Reomax STC1A250V instead of TBC1100A (out of stock); same 1 A time-lag rating.

L1.role: Keeps noise from the 5 V power module out of the mains

PS1.part: AC/DC power module, 90–245 VAC in, 5 V 2 A (10 W) out
PS1.role: Turns mains into safe, isolated 5 V for the whole board
PS1.note: Rated for 60 °C ambient; this module sets the board's 60 °C rating (every other part is chosen for 85 °C).

C2.role: Energy reservoir on the 5 V output of the power module
C2.note: Same 220 µF 16 V in a shorter can (6.3 × 7 mm instead of the 6.3 × 11 mm Koshin PKLH in the schematic link); fits the same footprint.

U30.part: Step-down converter chip, 5 V → 3.3 V, 2 A
U30.role: Makes the 3.3 V supply for processor, display and sensor chips

L30.role: Energy-storage coil of the 3.3 V converter

C124,C127,C330,C331.role: Smooth the 5 V input of the 3.3 V and backlight converters
C124,C127,C330,C331.note: C330/C331 at the 3.3 V converter input, C124/C127 in the backlight converter's input filter. Same part number as C116, C122, C336.

C333,C334.role: Smooth the 3.3 V output of the converter
C333,C334.note: Upgrade: 16 V instead of 10 V (the 10 V part is not in stock).

R330.role: Sets the converter's output to 3.3 V (together with R331)

R331.role: Sets the converter's output to 3.3 V (together with R330)

U31.role: Makes 1.2 V for the core of the display controller

Q1.part: Triac 25 A 800 V, insulated TO-220 (electronic power switch)
Q1.role: Switches the 1 kW heater on and off

U5.role: Lets the processor fire the triac while staying isolated from mains
U5.note: MOC3052 instead of MOC3053M (not stocked); it needs more LED current, hence R4 = 120 Ω. The KiCad value reads MOC3052M; the part bought is Isocom MOC3052X.

R4.role: Sets the current through the opto-triac's built-in LED
R4.note: 120 Ω instead of 200 Ω because U5 changed to the MOC3052. Already in the KiCad schematic since 2026-11-13; Rev3.0_BOM.csv was exported before that.

R2,R3.role: Limit the triac's trigger current on the mains side

C4.part: 10 nF 305 VAC X2 safety film capacitor
C4.role: With R5, softens voltage spikes across the triac

R5.role: With C4, softens voltage spikes across the triac

RV2.part: Varistor (surge absorber), 350 VAC class, 10 mm disc
RV2.role: Clamps surges across the triac to protect it

U1.role: Detects each mains zero crossing, isolated from the mains

R6,R7.role: Feed a tiny mains current into the zero-cross detector

U6.part: Single logic inverter with Schmitt-trigger input, SOT-23-5
U6.role: Turns the zero-cross pulse into a clean digital signal
U6.note: Bought SN74AHC1G14DBVR; schematic value is SN74LVC1G14DBVR. Same single Schmitt-trigger inverter and pinout. The sourced BOM does not mark this as a substitution.

R9.role: Series resistor on the zero-cross signal to the processor

K1.part: Relay, 5 V coil, changeover contact, 7 A
K1.role: Switches the oven fan on mains voltage
K1.note: Tianbo HJR-3FF instead of Songle SRD-05VDC-SL-C (not stocked); same footprint and pinout, 7 A contacts (the relay only switches the fan).

Q4.role: Lets the processor switch the relay coil current

D5.role: Absorbs the relay coil's voltage spike at switch-off
D5.note: 1N4148W (Panjit) instead of MMSD4148T1G (out of stock); same kind of diode.

R16.role: Limits the processor's drive current into the transistor

U3.part: ESP32-WROOM-32E module, Wi-Fi + Bluetooth, 16 MB flash
U3.role: Main processor: runs control, display, touch and Wi-Fi

C5,C8.role: Smooth the 3.3 V supply right at the processor
C5,C8.note: The schematic link was Viking MCF02KTB250104 (100 nF 25 V), out of stock; one Yageo 100 nF 50 V part is bought for every 100 nF 0402 place on the board.

C6.role: With a resistor, holds the processor in reset until power is stable
C6.note: Value changed 100 nF → 1 µF (owner decision 2026-11-13, Espressif's recommendation for the reset delay). The KiCad schematic shows 1 µF; Rev3.0_BOM.csv was exported before the change.

C7.role: Local energy reservoir for the processor's Wi-Fi current bursts

J2.role: Programming port for a USB-to-serial (FTDI) adapter

Q2,Q3.role: Let the programming adapter reset and restart the processor
Q2,Q3.note: MMBT4401 instead of S8050 (not stocked); same pinout, 600 mA 40 V.

R8,R10-R15,R124,R224.role: Hold control lines at a defined level when nothing drives them
R8,R10-R15,R124,R224.note: Used in several circuits: R8/R10 zero-cross signal, R11–R14 programming reset, R15 fan transistor, R124 display chip, R224 temperature chip.

R130,R131.role: Keep the data bus to touch and sensor chips at its idle level
R130,R131.note: Pull-up resistors of the two-wire I²C bus shared by the touch controller and the temperature converter.

U10.part: Display controller SSD1963 with picture memory, LQFP-128
U10.role: Stores the picture and drives the 7-inch screen

Y10.role: Clock reference for the display controller

C110,C111.role: Let the crystal run at exactly 10 MHz

R110-R121.role: Soften the fast data signals from processor to display chip

RN1-RN7.role: Soften the 28 picture signals to the screen, cutting radio interference

C112-C115,C117-C119,C123,C126,C223,C225,.role: Smooth the supply right at the display chip, screen, touch and sensor
C112-C115,C117-C119,C123,C126,C223,C225,.note: Upgrade: 50 V instead of 16 V, same 100 nF. C112–C115 and C117–C119 at the display chip, C123 screen supply, C126 touch supply, C223/C225/C226 temperature circuit.

C116,C122,C336.role: Larger smoothing capacitors on the display and 1.2 V supplies
C116,C122,C336.note: Upgrade: 10 V instead of 6.3 V. C116 at the display chip, C122 screen supply, C336 at the 1.2 V regulator output.

C120,C121,C337.role: Smooth the 1.2 V core supply of the display chip
C120,C121,C337.note: Upgrade: 16 V instead of 6.3 V. C120/C121 at the display chip's 1.2 V pins, C337 at the 1.2 V regulator output.

J10.part: 40-pin flat-cable (FPC) connector, 0.5 mm pitch, top contact
J10.role: Takes the screen's flat cable: picture signals and backlight power

J11.part: 6-pin flat-cable (FPC) connector, 0.5 mm pitch, top contact
J11.role: Takes the touch panel's flat cable

U11.role: Raises 5 V to about 9.6 V for the screen's LED backlight

L11.role: Energy-storage coil of the backlight converter

D111.part: Schottky diode SS14, 1 A 40 V, SMA
D111.role: One-way valve for current in the backlight converter
D111.note: Same SS14 type made by Jiaqi; the ON Semiconductor / Panjit versions are not stocked.

C125.note: 50 V X5R instead of 25 V X7R (no 25 V X7R 0805 in stock); the 50 V part keeps more of its capacitance at the 9.6 V it sees.

D114.role: Limits the voltage if the backlight is disconnected

R122,R123.role: Measure the backlight current so it stays at 138 mA
R122,R123.note: Precision 0.1 % thin-film part, the only 18 Ω 0805 in stock; better than needed.

R126,R128.role: Wire links in the backlight control path

R127.role: Keeps the backlight off until the display chip is ready

L12.role: Filter coil that keeps backlight noise off the 5 V supply
L12.note: 10 µH instead of 2.2 µH (the 2.2 µH part is not stocked); same part as L11, the filter still works (corner 34 → 16 kHz).

R132.role: Stops the backlight's input filter from oscillating (with C128)
R132.note: Upgrade: 1 % 0.5 W instead of 0.25 W. The sourced BOM names a cheaper 5 % 0.25 W alternative (Uniohm RR1206J050KT5E, 0.046 USD).

C128.part: 47 µF 16 V electrolytic capacitor, SMD 5 × 5.8 mm
C128.role: Stops the backlight's input filter from oscillating (with R132)
C128.note: Upgrade: 16 V instead of 10 V, can 5.8 mm tall instead of 5.4 mm, same footprint. Özdisan stock 316, enough for 100 boards.

C129,C332.role: Noise filter on the backlight wires; helper for the 3.3 V converter
C129,C332.note: Upgrade: 50 V instead of 25 V. C129 sits at the screen connector, C332 belongs to the 3.3 V converter.

C130-C133.role: Give radio-frequency noise a short path to ground at the connectors

R125,R129.role: Feed 3.3 V to the screen and to the touch panel

D112,D113,D115,D116,D220,D221.role: Protect touch and probe lines against static electricity
D112,D113,D115,D116,D220,D221.note: D112/D113/D115/D116 at the touch connector, D220/D221 at the thermocouple terminal.

U20.role: Measures the probe's tiny voltage very precisely

J20.role: Connection point for the thermocouple probe wires

TH220.role: Measures the terminal's own temperature to correct the reading
TH220.note: Thinking TSM1B103F3381RZ instead of Murata NCP18XH103F03RB (not stocked); same 10 kΩ 1 % B 3380 K in 0603.

R220,R221.role: Part of the noise filter on the probe input

C220.role: Filters noise between the two probe wires

C221,C222.role: Filter noise picked up equally on both probe wires
C221,C222.note: Less precise type: X7R 10 % instead of C0G 1 % (no 10 nF C0G 0603 in stock). The Design Specification §6 works the noise case with a 10 % mismatch; the sourced BOM calls it acceptable.

R222,R223.role: Make a disconnected or broken probe show up as an error

R225-R227.role: Reference resistors for the thermistor measurement

C224,C335.role: Smooth the supply of the converter chip and the 1.2 V regulator
C224,C335.note: C224 at the temperature converter chip, C335 at the 1.2 V regulator input. Same part number as C120, C121, C337.

HS1.part: Aluminium heatsink 45 × 12.7 × 63.5 mm with solder pins, for TO-220
HS1.role: Carries away the heater switch's heat, about 3.7 W
HS1.note: Not sold by Özdisan (its largest TO-220 heatsink is 35 mm); bought from DigiKey, minimum order 5.

F1/F3 clips.part: Fuse clip for 5 × 20 mm fuses, PCB mount
F1/F3 clips.role: Hold the two glass fuses so they can be replaced
F1/F3 clips.note: Not drawn in the schematic: 2 clips per fuse, 4 per board. The clip pin diameter against the 1.3 mm footprint holes is still to be confirmed.

TC1 (probe).part: K-type thermocouple probe, M6 ring tip, 1 m lead, 0–600 °C
TC1 (probe).role: Senses the oven temperature; its wires screw into J20
TC1 (probe).note: Motorobit shows stock '10+' against 100 needed: ask Motorobit for 100 pieces. Price 145.86 TL + VAT at 50.3 TL/USD (2026-11-12). Özdisan sells no thermocouple probes.

not_sourced.part: 1 kW heater element (part of the oven)
not_sourced.role: Heats the oven; switched on and off by the triac Q1
not_sourced.note: Oven-side part, not part of the electronics; there is no supplier line for it in the repo. It is soldered to the board's heater pads.

not_sourced.part: Solder pads for the mains cable (no part)
not_sourced.role: Where the mains cable (live and neutral) is soldered on
not_sourced.note: Nothing to buy: bare pads on the board.

not_sourced.part: Solder pads for the fan cable (no part)
not_sourced.role: Where the oven fan's cable is soldered on
not_sourced.note: Nothing to buy: bare pads on the board. The fan itself is an oven part.

not_sourced.role: Stands for the wall socket in circuit simulations only
not_sourced.note: Nothing to buy. The schematic's link for V1 points to the ngspice simulator manual, not to a product, so no link is given.

not_in_component_total.part: 7-inch TFT colour display, 800 × 480, with capacitive touch panel (GT911 touch controller)
not_in_component_total.role: The screen and touch surface behind the glass front
not_in_component_total.note: Single-piece price read 2026-11-09 (₺1,990 at about 50 TRY/USD, Design Specification §2); the repo has no 100-piece price. Özdisan stock was 61 then, below the 100 needed. Kept out of the component total on purpose, as in the sourced BOM. Rated −20…+70 °C.

not_in_component_total.part: Printed circuit board: 4 layers, 1.6 mm FR4, 1 oz copper, 183.6 × 118.6 mm including mounting ears
not_in_component_total.role: Carries and connects all the parts
not_in_component_total.note: No fabrication quote in the repo. The surface finish (ENIG) is still marked TBD in the fabrication notes (Design Specification §12.10).

not_in_component_total.part: Soldering all parts onto the board (surface-mount and through-hole) and testing
not_in_component_total.role: Turns the bare board and loose parts into a working controller
not_in_component_total.note: No assembly quote in the repo. About 146 pieces per board: mostly surface-mount, plus about 25 through-hole pieces (mains parts, power module, relay, heatsink, screw terminal, header, fuse clips).

not_in_component_total.part: Glass-front display module GF-2.1: printed strengthened cover glass, moulded frame, adhesives, fasteners
not_in_component_total.role: Holds the screen flush behind the glass in the oven's front panel
not_in_component_total.note: Desk estimate, no supplier quoted (Rev3.0_GlassFront_Design.md §0.3): recurring cost per oven 580 / 1,390 / 2,680 TRY (low / likely / high), i.e. $12 / $28 / $53; the likely $28 is shown. One-off mould, jigs and set-up (likely 246 k TRY for the first 100) and about 1 h of in-house labour per unit are extra.
